title: Rangoli Meenakari Rakhi — Green and Yellow Petals with Crystal Flower
shortDescription: A meenakari flower in green and yellow, set with red and white crystals, on maroon and gold beadwork.
description:
A full meenakari flower sits at the centre of this rakhi — pointed petals hand-enamelled in green and yellow, radiating out from a rosette of red and white crystals. On either side, faceted gold beads step down into maroon barrel beads, broken up by a single turquoise and a single amber bead. It is a busy, generous design in the old Rajasthani rangoli palette, and it reads from across a room.

Tied with a soft red silk thread with a knotted tassel, comfortable enough to keep on all day.

title: Suraj Chakra Rakhi — Orange Sunburst Disc with Coral and Pearl Beads
shortDescription: A glossy orange sunburst disc framed by coral, ruby-red and white pearl beads on a red-yellow mauli thread.
description:
The centre is a smooth domed disc printed with a fine orange-on-gold sunburst — dozens of rays running out from a single point, glazed over so it catches the light like enamel. Around it, small ruby-red faceted beads, coral seed beads and white pearls sit in tidy double rows, closed off with gold cone caps.

The thread is the traditional red-and-yellow twisted mauli rather than plain silk, which is what gives this one its temple feel. Light, flat and easy to wear.

title: Sunehri Daisy Rakhi — Carved Gold Flower with Orange and Green Jade Beads
shortDescription: A flat carved gold daisy between double rows of orange and green jade beads on a red silk thread.
description:
A single carved daisy in antique gold, its petals long and flat, with a ring of tiny raised dots around the centre. It is deliberately understated — no stones, no crystals, just the shape of the flower and the finish on the metal.

On either side, double rows of orange and deep green jade-look beads run out to gold cone caps. The colour pairing is the giveaway: marigold orange against temple green, the two colours of every Indian festival.

A good choice for a brother who does not wear anything flashy.

title: Muskaan Surya Rakhi — Smiling Sun with Ruby Crystals and Pearls
shortDescription: A gold sun with a smiling face, flanked by ruby-red crystals and rows of white pearls.
description:
A sun with a face on it — flame-shaped rays all around a smooth gold centre stamped with a small smile. It is a warm, cheerful design rather than a solemn one, and it is the one to send a younger brother, or a brother who would rather laugh than be sentimental.

Ruby-red faceted crystals sit on either side of the sun, then two neat rows of small white pearls, closed with ribbed gold caps. Bright red silk thread with a looped tassel.

title: Kundan Kamal Rakhi — Meenakari Lotus with Maroon and Gold Pearl Beads
shortDescription: A kundan lotus with green and yellow enamelled petals, on twin rows of maroon beads and gold pearls.
description:
The centre is a kundan lotus: six petals set with clear stones around a raised stone heart, ringed by hand-enamelled meenakari petals in green and yellow. It is the most worked piece in the range, and the one that looks the most like jewellery.

The arms are built up in twin rows of small maroon beads, punctuated by large gold-finish pearls and faceted gold spacers, tapering out to a fine red thread with a beaded tassel at each end.

If you want the rakhi itself to be the gift, this is the one.
